source.title: Selective Amnesia: On Efficient, High-Fidelity and Blind Suppression of Backdoor Effects in Trojaned Machine Learning Models
source.authors: Rui Zhu; Di Tang; Si-Yuan Tang; Xiao-Feng Wang; Haixu Tang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses random-label training as the forgetting step in its SEAM backdoor-unlearning method, then evaluates backdoor suppression and primary-task recovery. It does not test the catalog claims about fitting random labels as a standalone training outcome.
record.gate_note: Random-label training is described as part of SEAM, but the paper reports no standalone random-label training error, test error, or label-noise convergence result. The CIFAR10 random-label experiment varies the fraction of randomly wrong labels and reports resulting primary-task ACC and backdoor ASR; these outcomes measure induced forgetting for backdoor removal, not the claim versions' named outcomes. Other SEAM efficacy and comparison results are about backdoor defenses and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: SEAM uses random-label retraining to induce forgetting and evaluates clean-task accuracy, backdoor success and recovery. It reports no accuracy on the assigned random labels, convergence to random-label interpolation, or mixed-label learning trajectories. Its results therefore do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that random-label retraining induces forgetting of primary and backdoor tasks, followed by clean-data retraining that selectively restores primary-task performance. They characterize SEAM as suppressing backdoor effects through partial unlearning; backdoor traces can remain and later revive.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly wrong labels are used as the forgetting phase of a two-step backdoor-unlearning pipeline, followed by recovery training on correctly labeled clean data; the paper does not reproduce standalone random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery dataset size and attack type change SEAM's reported backdoor-suppression and clean-accuracy outcomes; these are not outcomes for the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.3 and Figure 1 report that a backdoored CIFAR10 VGG16, initially at 92% clean accuracy and 99% attack success, loses both capabilities as 100–1000 of 1000 clean examples receive randomly wrong labels during one epoch of retraining. Both measures reportedly approach zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing randomly wrong supervision during brief retraining of a pretrained backdoored network can increase forgetting of its clean and backdoor tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 and Figure 2 report greater preservation of shallow-layer representations than output-adjacent representations after random-label forgetting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label retraining used for forgetting can preserve shallow representations while changing deeper representations.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (2023 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP))
record.problems: The random-label experiment reports ACC and ASR changes in Fig. 1 without numerical values in the text; it varies the fraction of samples assigned randomly wrong labels, rather than measuring training error or test error for random-label fitting.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: reported SEAM backdoor-unlearning results do not measure an outcome named by V1–V6. Fig. 1 reports primary-task ACC and backdoor ASR during the forgetting step, not random-label training or test error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on a fixed, completely random labeling, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fitting alongside steadily worsening test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels during training.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping rows and verdicts empty is appropriate. Algorithm 1 regenerates randomly wrong labels each epoch and stops based on accuracy against clean labels, rather than demonstrating interpolation of a fixed random labeling. Figure 1's clean-test accuracy decline alone does not establish V4, and sequential forgetting followed by recovery does not establish V6.

versions.untested_parts: Standalone training error and test error after random labeling, with the original architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison for fitting random versus true labels, and convergence speed as corrupted-label fraction grows.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training error and test error across a sweep from no label corruption to all labels corrupted.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
